The killer is IDENTIFIED from evidence already on the box — recorded here so the

**Prime suspect confirmed: `earlyoom` under its blanket python `--prefer` bonus.**

1. VM timezone is `America/Los_Angeles` (PDT, UTC-7), so journal local times map
   directly onto the body's UTC incident stamps.
2. Window A — body reports `issue2221_build_mix.py` attempt 1 died rc=143 at
   16:24:40Z. The earlyoom unit journal has, at `Aug 13 09:24:40` PDT (= the same
   second): `mem avail: 12849 of 128804 MiB (9.98%)`, `low memory! at or below
   SIGTERM limits`, then `sending SIGTERM to process 1838073 uid 1001 "python3":
   badness 972, VmRSS 1054 MiB`. Same second, same signal, matching victim class.
3. Window B — body reports two `scripts/file_infra_task.py` kills at ~00:42-44Z on
   2026-08-14 (= 17:42-44 PDT on 08-13). The journal shows a sustained sweep across
   that window: `"python"` at badness 973 (VmRSS 1395 MiB), then `"python3"` at
   badness 966 (VmRSS 53 MiB), 966 (48 MiB), and a `chrome` at 800 — all SIGTERM,
   all inside 11 seconds, with MemAvailable oscillating at 9.47-10.00%.
4. Mechanism — live config `/etc/default/earlyoom`:
   `EARLYOOM_ARGS="-m 10 -s 10 -r 3600 --prefer (^|/)(pytest|python3?)$ --avoid (^|/)(sshd|systemd|dockerd|node|claude|happy)$|^[0-9]+[.][0-9]+[.][0-9]+$ -n"`.
   The `--prefer` +300 badness bonus applies to every process whose comm matches
   `pytest` / `python` / `python3`, which INVERTS size ordering: an observed 44 MiB
   python scores badness 966, beating a 3728 MiB java (686) and a 660 MiB Claude
   session (670). So under the 10%-MemAvailable floor every python on the box is a
   top-priority victim regardless of how small or short-lived it is.

**Why the body's own checks missed it (three traps to carry into the plan):**

- "No OOM (journalctl clean)" — the kernel OOM killer logs to dmesg with
  `oom_score`; earlyoom logs to its own unit journal with `badness`. A dmesg /
  kernel-log read structurally cannot see an earlyoom kill. (Already the documented
  protocol: `failure_patterns.md` § exit-137/143 step 3, `gotchas.md` line 61.)
- "53 GB free" is DISK; the binding quantity is MemAvailable, which was at 9.5-10.0%
  of 128 GB (~12.2-12.9 GB) in both windows.
- The `setsid`-survives / in-session-dies discriminator is almost certainly a
  CONFOUND, not a mechanism: earlyoom selects on badness and is session-agnostic —
  it never inspects session or process-group membership. earlyoom fires in bursts at
  the floor, so a rerun seconds-to-minutes later lands outside the sweep and
  survives. Any survive-vs-die A/B on this VM is uninterpretable unless both arms
  run inside one sweep window. This trap is what pointed the original triage at
  harness child-reaping / janitor pkill / systemd session cleanup.
